Subject: Internal: proposed redlines for NovaMetrics renewal (preliminary)

Team — putting initial legal notes here so were aligned before we send a consolidated redline to NovaMetrics. This is an internal thread.

Summary of material asks from customer: 18-month term, +25% committed capacity, smaller adjustments to data retention and SLA credits.

High-level suggestions (draft language to follow):
- Section 4.2 (SLA credits): keep formula but cap total credits at 25% of monthly fees; add an exception carve-out for scheduled maintenance > 24 hours with prior notice.
- Section 5.4 (Data retention): propose 90 days default retention for logs, 365 days for backup snapshots; for regulated data we require a signed DPA addendum (we should attach as Exhibit G).
- Liability / Indemnity (Section 7.1): adjust Redwoods liability cap to 1x annualized committed fees for the renewal term; customer asked for higher — recommend we hold firm to preserve enterprise pooling.
- Order form / exhibits: add a short Exhibit H titled "Capacity Ramp & Burst" documenting burst rates, ramp windows, and billing for overages. This keeps technical detail out of the main MSA.

Please review the attached suggested redline (proposed-msaredline.docx) — it contains exact markup and a short rationale for each change. Notable points I want alignment on before we go to NovaMetrics:
1) Are we willing to offer a 15% one-time credit if they sign a 18-month term? (sales incentive)
2) Pricing tiers: if we accept 25% committed uplift, do we rebate at the new tier immediately or pro-rate over first 3 months?

Marissa — can you confirm whether finance is ok with either the 15% incentive or pro-rate approach? Karthik — weigh-in on whether Exhibit H covers all technical ramp details so we dont leave open ambiguity.

Attachments: proposed-msaredline.docx

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed your note and the proposed checklist. A few quick counters from our side:

- Term length: were not comfortable committing to 18 months. Our procurement standard is 12 months; we can consider 15 months if Redwood agrees to a small invoice credit in month 1.
- Data deletion: well accept retention windows as proposed but need explicit deletion language for end-of-term data handling; prefer data deletion within 30 days of termination for customer PII (we can accept 90 days for logs).
- SLA credits: acceptable with a cap, but request a longer notice window for scheduled maintenance (48 hours) and a short review clause to revisit SLAs at 12 months.

Attached are our counters with tracked changes. Well prepare a DocuSign packet once we land language on the term and order form.

Attachments: NM_Counter_Redlines.docx
